subject: Commercial — capacity option & deferred billing ladder (Globex Health RFI)
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@globexhealth.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference.com, procurements@globexhealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI — commercial clarification (capacity options / deferred billing)

Sofia / Redwood team,

Thanks for the product questionnaire you returned last week — it was helpful. Procurement at Globex has one follow-up on the commercial section before we build the scoring matrix: we need a short, explicit section describing the pricing construct you propose if a customer wants a) guaranteed reserved capacity for steady-state throughput, and b) an option to defer a portion of payment to the following quarter in exchange for a modest rate premium or service credit (we have finance constraints for Q4).

Specific asks:
- Tiered commit bands (annual token commit) and the per-unit pricing for each band (please show math example).
- Overage rate mechanics and whether credits/roll-forward apply.
- A ‘deferred billing ladder’ — describe how deferred invoices would be scheduled, any fees or credits for deferral, and the maximum roll-forward period.
- Any discounts tied to sustainability or use of lower-carbon GPU pools (we have a green procurement requirement).
- Sample invoice cadence and a short example invoice for a quarter that hits 120% of committed usage.

We attached the RFI excerpt for your reference. Can we get a short commercial appendix by EOD Wednesday (PST)? Procurement will include the answer in their vendor comparison.

Best,
Elena
Elena Moreno
VP Procurement — Globex Health
procurements@globexhealth.com

Subject: Re: RFI — commercial clarification (capacity options / deferred billing)

Team — forwarding Elastix RFI note. They need a concise commercial appendix that covers reserved capacity + a deferred billing ladder. They want examples and a sample invoice. We should keep numbers illustrative but defensible; procurement may push back on complexity, so present a baseline + one optional add-on (deferred ladder).

Proposed structure for reply (short appendix + bullet examples):
1) Pricing summary table: annual commit bands (0-50M, 50-200M, 200M+ tokens) with per-1M token list prices and equivalent per-1k token metrics.
2) Reserved capacity option: monthly committed throughput (vGPU pool) with guaranteed QPS and dedicated baseline price (expressed as effective per-token when amortized).
3) Overage policy: tiered overage (charged at 125% of list per-unit for first 20% over; 150% thereafter) + 30-day invoice credit if average burst > 200% (to protect sudden spikes).
4) Deferred billing ladder: allow up to 40% of an invoice to be deferred to the next quarter with a 1.5% finance fee per month deferred OR an alternative: 0% fee plus a 2% service-credit if customer accepts deferred billing and provides payment guarantee (escrow). Max deferral 2 quarters.
5) Sustainability discount: 2% rebate on committed spend if customer consumes ≥60% of tokens on our verified low-carbon GPU pool (tracked via billing tags).

Marcus / Laura / Neha — please comment on numbers and whether the deferred ladder option is ok operationally. I’ve attached a draft pricing workbook.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI — commercial clarification (capacity options / deferred billing)

Quick edits on numbers — trying to keep the reply conservative but attractive. I recommend we show both the nominal per-unit list price and an amortized effective cost for Reserved Capacity so finance can compare apples-to-apples. Proposed example figures (illustrative):

Pricing table (annual commit, effective per-1M tokens):
- Band A: 0 - 50M: list $1,200 per 1M tokens (=$0.0012 per token).
- Band B: 50M - 200M: list $900 per 1M tokens (=$0.0009 per token).
- Band C: 200M+: list $650 per 1M tokens (=$0.00065 per token).

Reserved capacity example (24/7 dedicated pool, 4x A100-equivalent vGPUs):
- Monthly reserved fee: $48,000 (covers baseline throughput ~12B tokens/month).
- Amortized effective price: $48,000 / 12B = $0.000004 per token baseline. When combined with prompt/response overhead and load, show effective blended price of ~$0.00075 per token at 10B/mo usage.

Overage mechanics: first 20% over commit charged at 125% of list per-1M; amounts >120% charged at 150% of list per-1M. Credits: unused commit in a quarter can be rolled forward once (applies only to Band B/C) OR applied as invoice credit; roll-forward cap = 25% of original commit.

Deferred billing ladder (operational notes):
- Option A (fee): customer may defer up to 40% of quarterly invoice to next quarter at 1.5% per month (simple interest). Max defer = 2 quarters.
- Option B (service-credit): no finance fee if customer accepts 2% service-credit applied to next invoice and provides payment guarantee (PO with escrow).
- Implementation: billing team issues 'deferred invoice note' and creates a deferred balance line; docusign SOW amendment required.

Sustainability discount: 2% rebate applied as a post-invoice credit if tagged consumption on low-carbon pools ≥60% for the quarter. We will provide verified consumption report for audit.

If team agrees, I’ll draft the appendix and sample invoice.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Commercial Pricing — Redwood Inference

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference.com <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI — commercial clarification (capacity options / deferred billing)

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise commercial appendix addressing the items in your RFI and a sample invoice illustrating a quarter with 120% usage. Highlights below and next steps: 

1) Commit bands & list pricing (per 1M tokens): Band A (0-50M): $1,200; Band B (50-200M): $900; Band C (200M+): $650. We included per-token equivalents in the appendix for clarity.

2) Reserved Capacity option: offered as a monthly reserved fee (example: $48,000/mo for a 4x A100-equivalent pool) — we show an amortized effective per-token rate in the appendix so you can compare it to list pricing.

3) Overage policy: overage charged at 125% of list for <=20% over; 150% thereafter. We offer one roll-forward of unused quarterly commit (cap 25% of quarterly commit) as an invoice credit applied to the subsequent quarter.

4) Deferred billing ladder: two options — (A) fee-based deferral (up to 40% deferred to next quarter, 1.5% monthly finance fee, max 2 quarters) or (B) service-credit deferral (0% finance fee, 2% credit, requires payment guarantee/escrow). Implementation requires a one-page SOW amendment; billing will surface a deferred balance on the invoice.

5) Sustainability rebate: 2% rebate on committed spend if you elect to route >=60% of workload to our low-carbon GPU pool (we include tags and a verified consumption report each quarter).

Attachments: commercial appendix (PDF), RI_Pricing_Workbook_Globex_v1.xlsx, Draft_SOW_capacity-option.docx

Next steps: if this aligns with procurement’s scoring, we can produce a one-page SOW amendment and a sample DocuSign envelope for the deferral option you prefer. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the appendix Thursday morning PST.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference.com
